sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press. xvii+253 pp. (Zenodo 5688969, CC-BY)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Sasaru. Sasaru is named only on pp.10-11 ('most likely North-Central Edoid peoples: Ososo, Ate, Ikpeshi, Sasaru, and Enwan, all of Akoko-Edo') and in the classification list p.24 '(h) Igwe-Enwa-Sasaru', 'left out of the family tree because their exact relationship with the rest of NCE has not been determined'. No Sasaru sketch in ch.4, no Sasaru forms in the lexicon; the word 'stress' occurs nowhere in the book.
